chunks: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: This is confirmed by the Book of Allāh.
About praying, Allāh says: “Call you to Me, I will answer you”
About forgiveness Allāh says: “And whoever does evil, or wrongs his own self and thereafter seeks pardon of Allāh, shall find Allāh Oft-forgiving, Merciful”
About gratefulness He says: “If you be grateful I will increase (my favours) to you”

About repentance He says: “Verily, repentance (acceptable) with Allāh is only for those who do evil ignorantly and then turn (to Allāh) soon (after); these (are those) Allāh will turn (merciful) to them; and Allāh is All-knowing, All-wise”
ai.seo_question: How does the Quran link human actions like gratitude and repentance to divine response?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Raḍī structures this passage to demonstrate the reciprocal nature of the covenant between God and humanity, emphasizing that divine grace is contingent upon human initiative. This selection highlights the theological principle that God’s attributes of Mercy (Rahmah), Generosity (Fadl), and Acceptance (Qabul) are actively triggered by the believer's specific acts of worship, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the efficacy of sincere supplication and repentance.

en.sayed-ali-raza: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: This is confirmed by the Book of Allāh.
About praying, Allāh says: “Call you to Me, I will answer you” (Qur’ān, 40:60).
About forgiveness Allāh says: “And whoever does evil, or wrongs his own self and thereafter seeks pardon of Allāh, shall find Allāh Oft-forgiving, Merciful” (Qur’ān, 4:110).
About gratefulness He says: “If you be grateful I will increase (my favours) to you” (Qur’ān, 14:7).

About repentance He says: “Verily, repentance (acceptable) with Allāh is only for those who do evil ignorantly and then turn (to Allāh) soon (after); these (are those) Allāh will turn (merciful) to them; and Allāh is All-knowing, All-wise” (Qur’ān, 4:17).
